analysis.headline: Cross-Asset Rotation Analysis: Thematic Technology and European Leaders Maintain Persistence Amid Sector Divergences
analysis.market_regime: Selective Leadership with Within-Sector Divergence and Mixed-Horizon Transitions
analysis.executive_summary: Quantitative ETF rotation tracking indicates sustained strength in select software and cloud technology themes alongside European equity markets, while broad US sector benchmarks demonstrate mixed-horizon signals. Cloud Computing (SKYY) stands out as a persistent leader with a score of 98.65, while defensive sectors such as Utilities (XLU) and Consumer Staples (PBJ) show systematic rotation-out characteristics. Significant sector divergences exist within Health Care, Industrials, Technology, and Consumer Discretionary, where sub-industry performance diverges sharply from broad sector trends.

cross_market_confirmations: Global Materials leadership (MXI, score 67.50, 20-bar score change 49.00) confirms US Materials emerging momentum (XLB, score 65.56, 20-bar score change 40.56) and industry-level strength in Metals & Mining (XME, score 63.85, 20-bar score change 45.14).

risks_or_conflicts: Health Care sector divergence: Medical Devices (IHI, score 75.19, 20-bar score change 35.19) exhibits strong improvement while Health Care Providers (IHF, score 41.54, 20-bar score change -39.20, at a 63-bar score low) deteriorates.

Industrials sector divergence: Aerospace & Defense (ITA, score 64.23, 20-bar score change 36.82) shows relative improvement while Transportation (IYT, score 28.65, 20-bar score change -29.49, at a 63-bar score low) suffers sharp weakness.

Information Technology sector divergence: Software (IGV, score 75.58, 20-bar score change 36.32) accelerates while Semiconductors (SMH, score 34.42, 20-bar score change -22.06) experiences severe weakness.
Consumer Discretionary sector divergence: Leisure & Entertainment (PEJ, score 51.92, 20-bar score change 18.03) improves while Retail (XRT, score 46.73, 20-bar score change -23.45) deteriorates.

Pair state tension in REET vs XLRE: Global REITs (REET) carries a confirmed WEAKENING cross-sectional state (score 49.11) while maintaining a confirmed PAIR_LEADING signal versus XLRE based on a 63-bar pair spread of 0.82 percentage points, with a pending PAIR_MIXED condition (2/3 observations).
analysis.methodology_note: Interpretation uses Python-confirmed trend states that require 3 consecutive daily observations before a new raw condition becomes canonical. Raw conditions remain available as pending early warnings. Evidence also uses deterministic 5-bar score changes, 20- and 63-bar relative strength or pair spreads, persistence metrics, and Python-calculated attention flags including 63-bar rotation-score extrema and material cross-market conflicts. ETF volume and CMF are treated as market-participation indicators, not fund-flow data.
